title: Kripke semantics for intuitionistic first-order logic

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Syntax and semantics of predicate logic; Natural Deduction (handout 8)

summary: Interpret constructive first-order proofs in varying domains, with coherent object transports, persistent forcing and explicit quantifier witnesses.
abstract: Every object currently available may have a property even though a later stage introduces an object without it. This matters when a universal claim must remain justified as information grows, while an existence claim still needs a witness available now. We give first-order models with a domain at each stage and coherent maps carrying old objects forward. Their forcing relation respects substitution and preserves every intuitionistic deduction rule, including equality. A two-stage example separates present witnesses from future objects and refutes classical reasoning about an existential statement; single-stage models recover ordinary classical truth.
